title: issues/backlog _num concatenates digits from the id TAG, causing runaway ids and MAX_PATH store-write failures (close-loop test crash)
body: IS-TESTBIPF02-0002 was numbered 20002 because the tag 'TESTBIPF02' contains '02'. Repeated creates inflated the number until the item filename exceeded 260 chars and the write failed. Surfaced during a full develop precheck.

rcca.root_cause: issues._num/backlog._num extract the sequence via re.sub(r'\D','',id), which concatenates ALL digits in the id - including digits embedded in the TAG/slug (e.g. tag 'TESTBIPF02' contributes '02'). The next id is then mx+1 over that inflated number, producing a runaway id and, eventually, a >260-char filename (Windows MAX_PATH) that crashes the store write.
five_why: 1. Why did the close-loop test fail? raise_issue could not write items/<id>.json: FileNotFoundError.
2. Why was the path too long? The generated issue id was ~250 chars (e.g. IS-TESTBIPF02-2222...0126).
3. Why was the id that long? _next_id used _num() over existing ids; _num concatenates ALL digits.
4. Why did the tag add digits? tag_for slugifies the project name; '_test_bi_pf_0271' -> 'TESTBIPF02' (has '02').
5. Why did this compound? Each create re-inflated mx, so the number grew every write (runaway).
rcca.corrective: Parse the numeric SEQUENCE only: take the substring after the last '-' (the <nnn> segment) and read its digits; never concatenate digits from the tag. Apply to both core/issues.py and core/backlog.py (same defect class).
rcca.preventive: Add a guard test asserting id numbering is stable for tag-containing ids and that generated ids keep a bounded length; the existing wired_audit destructive/backlog integrity checks stay in place.
